Thank you for reaching out about the login issue you are experiencing. Based on our documentation, here are some common causes and steps you can try to resolve the "invalid credentials" message despite using a password manager:

1. Account Lockout: After five consecutive failed login attempts, accounts are locked for 30 minutes. Please check the security page of the console for a red banner indicating a lockout. If locked, wait 30 minutes or have an administrator unlock it from the team members page.
2. Stale Session Cookies: Sometimes, old session cookies interfere with login. Please clear your browser cookies for the CloudServe domain or try logging in using a private/incognito browsing window.
3. Cached Credentials in CLI: If you are using the CLI, run `cloudserve auth logout` followed by `cloudserve auth login` to clear cached tokens.
4. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): If MFA is enabled on your account, issues such as device clock drift or lost authenticator devices can cause login failures even with the correct password. Please ensure the device generating your authenticator codes has automatic time synchronization enabled. If you have lost your device or recovery codes, an administrator can reset MFA for you, or you may need to verify your identity with support if you are the sole administrator.

If none of these steps resolve your issue, I am not able to confirm additional causes from our documentation — a member of our team will follow up to assist further. Please let us know if you need help with any of the above steps or have additional details to share.

Thank you for reaching out regarding the increase in your invoice this month. There are several common reasons why an invoice might be higher than usual, including usage-based charges exceeding your plan allowance, resources running in staging or development environments that are billed at the same rate as production, or the billing period dates differing from the calendar month since billing runs from your subscription anniversary date.

To understand the increase, please review the usage breakdown for the billing period, which itemizes charges by service and environment. Check if any resources were left running in non-production environments, as these incur charges at the same rate as production. Also, verify the billing period dates at the top of your invoice to ensure you are comparing the correct timeframe.

If you have recently changed your plan, note that upgrades are prorated for the remainder of the billing period and appear as separate line items, while downgrades take effect at the start of the next period. Credits from downgrades or adjustments are usually applied to the next invoice rather than refunded immediately.

Additionally, if your usage exceeded your plan allowance, overage charges may have been applied. It is also possible that a spend cap was configured and reached, which can affect service and billing. We recommend setting usage alerts at 50%, 80%, and 95% of your allowance to monitor usage proactively.
